text:
kai: seeing a spike of targets getting kicked from the edge LB in us-west-2, started ~15:20 UTC. ALB shows 'Unhealthy' with 502/connection reset counts rising. Anyone else?

deploy-bot: New deploy to the edge-ingress group succeeded at 15:18 UTC — no automatic rollbacks.

maria: I can reproduce via curl from a pod in the same AZ: intermittent RSTs during keepalive handshake. Not an app 5xx.

ash: quick check: kube readiness probes are green per kubectl. Pods report Ready=true.

infra-oncall: grabbing LB logs and ENI metrics now. If targets are healthy from kube POV, could be NAT/egress or TCP reset from our side.

jess: throwing this here: we had a NAT gateway maintenance earlier today, but it finished before 14:00. No config changes after that AFAIK.

kai: attaching short snippet of ALB target log that shows resets: 
```
2026-03-17T15:22:01Z target=10.2.7.14:8080 status=502 reason=downstream_reset
2026-03-17T15:22:02Z target=10.2.6.9:8080 status=502 reason=downstream_reset
```

ash: does the ingress sidecar have any error lines? envoy metrics maybe?

maria: envoy logs: occasional 'connection error: connection reset by peer' from upstream cluster. No 5xx from app.

tom: could be ephemeral port exhaustion on the nodes handling LB probes -> LB TCP connection can't be established and ALB marks it unhealthy. Check conntrack /proc and ephemeral port allocation.

infra-oncall: running quick checks: `ss -tan state CLOSE-WAIT` counts are high on a subset of nodes. conntrack table usage at ~86% on those nodes.

jess: that points to NAT/egress port reuse. But ALB healthchecks are inbound -> why would egress ports matter? Are we terminating probes via a proxy that egresses?

kai: our edge setup: ALB -> nodePort -> envoy sidecar -> pod. Envoy makes upstream connections; if upstream path has SNAT (egress), connection reuse matters. Some nodes have a misconfigured iptables rule that causes SYNs to be reset when conntrack is near capacity.

ash: found a node with nf_conntrack_max accidentally set low (262144) because of a boot script regression. Most nodes are 524288. Changing it on the node immediately reduced CLOSE-WAITs.

maria: we patched the startup script cluster-wide for the autoscaling group to ensure correct nf_conntrack_max, and applied a rolling restart to the problematic node pool.

tom: also saw high TIME_WAIT counts from probe-to-upstream connections. Suggests keepalive settings: LB health check interval is 10s, but upstream idle timeout is 60s leading to many sockets in TIME_WAIT. We should tune keepalive or enable reuse.

infra-oncall: immediate mitigation applied: bumped nf_conntrack_max via daemonset on the node pool and reduced ALB healthcheck interval to 15s for affected target group to lower probe concurrency while we stabilize.

jess: long-term: add node-exporter alert for conntrack util > 70% and verify kernel settings in our AMI bake pipeline. Also add a post-deploy check for any boot script changes that touch sysctl.

kai: action items: 
- infra-oncall: confirm all nodes have nf_conntrack_max=524288 and roll remaining pools (ETA 30m)
- ash: check envoy idle/keepalive upstream settings and propose tune (ETA 2h)
- tom: add alert for TIME_WAIT surge tied to healthcheck windows (ETA EOD)
- jess: update AMI job and bake tests (ETA tomorrow)

maria: health checks stabilized after the daemonset bump, targets returned to InService ~15:28 UTC. Leaving monitoring on. :thumbsup:

kai: thanks team. If anything flares, ping oncall and we can reopen.
